chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Imran ibn al-Hajjaj al-Sabi'i, from Muhammad ibn Walid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever commits a sin, and knows that Allah is watching over it, if He wills He punishes him, and if He wills He forgives him; He forgives him even if he does not seek forgiveness.'
ai.seo_question: Does Allah forgive sins without the sinner seeking forgiveness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the profound mercy of Allah, noting that awareness of His watchfulness (*munaẓẓir*) can lead to forgiveness even without explicit supplication (*istighfar*). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tawbah* (repentance) as an internal state of consciousness rather than merely a ritualistic act, underscing that divine grace often precedes human effort.
